You see a garden wicket.
New timber braces hold the hinges true. The wicket can be opened and closed.

Timber rails span a hinged gap. Sound hinges let the wicket open and close; damaged ones can be braced with two salvaged timber. The longer path around remains open. Breaking the rails leaves a permanent opening. A drawgourd bed lies north of this shelter wall. Its ripe shell carries water; keep its seed for the prepared bed. A loose pallet in the supply cellar can provide timber if dismantled. The path around the west end stays open.
